newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's KCRC sees housing development along West rail.
newsitem.headline: HK's KCRC sees housing development along West rail.

text.p: Hong Kong's Kowloon-Canton Railway Corp said on Tuesday that property development along phase one of the territory's planned West rail line could provide 35 million square feet of residential accomodation area.

"It would come as no surprise to find that we could be dealing with some 45 million square feet of accomodation when it is all finished, of which perhaps some 35 million square feet or 78 percent might be residential," Chairman K.Y. Yeung said.
Yeung said the numbers were a very rough estimate since the company did not know how much land the government would grant, and had not determined the development mix of each site.

Government radio reported the development along the line could provide 44,000 flats over a seven year period. There will be nine stations and one depot along the line, of which seven would provide opportunities for overhead development, it said.
The proposed rail line would link the northwestern New Territories and central Kowloon, with construction anticipated to begin in mid-1998.
